## Code Review

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | 9 | All 12 acceptance criteria are addressed. The count query reads the same `v_transactions_internal_alive` view as the "Show unused payees" filter, so merged payees count toward their target, deleted transactions are left out, and unused payees are guaranteed to show `0` / `Never`. Replacing the old client-side guess at the unused list after a merge with a server refetch is a real fix. One gap is in the process: #149's five Open Questions (splits, future dates, schedules, clickable count, date format) were decided in the PR, but #149 has no record of those decisions. The PR calls them "agreed" rules without saying where they were agreed. Please write the decisions on #149 so the issue matches what was built. |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | 8 | The tests are strong. There are 12 server tests covering zero, multiple, deleted, merged, split (three cases), transfer, future-date and unused-list consistency, plus 5 tests for the display helper. Mutation score is 100%, and breaking the SQL by hand (`COUNT(*)`) confirmed the split tests catch it. Both test files pass locally (18/18). Gaps, all disclosed in the PR: no tests for the refetch logic after merge, undo or sync. AC9 (counts up to date after adding or deleting a transaction elsewhere), AC11 (page stays usable while loading) and undoing a delete (part of AC10) weren't checked at all, even by hand. |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | Clean and small: SQL in `db`, a thin handler, a pure display helper, and column widths shared between header and rows. The header also now accounts for the scrollbar width, which keeps the columns aligned. Issues: (1) **CI's `knip` check fails** because [`merge-stryker-reports.mjs`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/e614d05008967772550245d8d6d37f43231b71f3/docs/sprint3/mutation/scripts/merge-stryker-reports.mjs) isn't imported by anything and isn't listed as an entry point. knip passes on master, so merging as-is would make master's CI fail for everyone. Fix: in the root workspace of `knip.json`, set `"entry": ["bin/*.mts", "docs/**/scripts/*.mjs"]`. (2) [`payeeUsageDisplay.ts:53`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/e614d05008967772550245d8d6d37f43231b71f3/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/payeeUsageDisplay.ts#L53) uses `String(stats.count)`, so 1,234 transactions shows as `1234` with no locale grouping. (3) Nit: the `useCallback` in [`ManagePayeesWithData.tsx:45`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/e614d05008967772550245d8d6d37f43231b71f3/packages/desktop-client/src/components/payees/ManagePayeesWithData.tsx#L45) isn't needed under the React Compiler, which AGENTS.md says to rely on. |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | 9 | Excellent description: the design decision with alternatives, both new and existing tech debt, and a table matching each acceptance criterion to its tests. The comments explain why, for example why there's no `placeholderData` and why both queries are refetched together. One stale detail: the Test Evidence table still says the VRT screenshots are "pending regeneration", but the bot regenerated them in e614d05 and visual regression now passes. Please update AC1 and AC7 to say so. |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 9 | Strong. The PR title and every commit have the `[AI]` prefix, the self-review box is checked, and an AI log is included. The PR says plainly that all 17 tests were written by Claude Code and that their expected values came from the acceptance criteria, not the code's output. The mutation write-up separates what the AI did from what the author decided and lists independent checks: the broken-SQL test, comparing the mutants before and after, and checking merge, undo and alignment by hand in the demo budget. The only weakness is the Open Questions point above: the author says they made those decisions, but they're recorded only in the AI log and the mutation write-up, not where reviewers would look. |
| Overall — would you merge this as-is? | 8 | Almost. Before merging: (1) fix the `knip` failure so CI is green, (2) write the Open Question decisions on #149, and (3) update the stale VRT wording in Test Evidence. It would also be worth checking AC9 and undoing a delete by hand, since nothing covers them yet. Formatting the count by locale is a nice-to-have. |

```text
Written for: your TA and teammates reading the PR description or sprint deliverable.

## What the changes do and why

**Why:** the Payees table showed only names and rule counts, so you couldn't tell which duplicate payee to keep or which ones were stale without opening each one.

**What:**
- **Server:** a new query returns each payee's transaction count and last-used date. It reads the same data as the "Show unused payees" filter, so deleted transactions are left out and merged payees count toward their target.
- **UI:** new **Transactions** and **Last Used** columns. Payees with no transactions show `0` / `Never` in muted text, and `…` shows while loading.
- **Refresh:** the counts and the unused-payees list reload together after a merge, an undo or a sync. This also fixed two existing gaps: undo used to ignore transaction changes, and merges updated the unused list by guessing on the client instead of asking the server.
- **Tests, mutation testing reports and a release note.**

## Most important design decision

**Decision:** keep the unused-payees list and the new counts as two queries that read the same data, and always reload them together. This was the issue's main risk: the numbers had to agree with the unused filter and with merged payees.

**Alternatives:**
- **One combined server call:** guaranteed consistency, but it means changing the existing unused-payees code, which is a bigger and riskier change.
- **Work out "unused" from the counts on the client:** this would quietly change what "unused" means (e.g. payees referenced by rules), and that's out of scope.
- **Count from a different query:** this would duplicate the rules for deleted and merged rows, and risk the two disagreeing.

**Trade-off:** the two queries can briefly disagree while one has reloaded and the other hasn't.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: two new columns in the right place | Payees VRT screenshot (pending regeneration); manual check | E2E / manual | AC text |
| AC2: counts non-deleted transactions; merges count toward target | Server tests: counting, deleted transactions, merges, splits | Unit | AC text; agreed split rule |
| AC3: latest date in the user's format | Server latest/future-date tests; helper date-format tests | Unit | AC text; agreed future-date rule |
| AC4: `0` / `Never`, muted | Server "no transactions" test; helper "unused" test | Unit | AC text |
| AC5: unused payees show `0` / `Never` | Server test comparing stats with the unused list | Unit | AC text |
| AC6: transfer payees counted | Server transfer-payee test | Unit | AC text |
| AC7: right-aligned tabular numbers | Manual check; VRT once regenerated | Manual | AC text |
| AC8: merge updates without reload | Server merge test; manual check | Unit + manual | AC text |
| AC9: up to date after transaction changes | Server deleted-transaction test | Unit (data only) | AC text |
| AC10: undo restores counts | Manual check (merge undo) | Manual | AC text |
| AC11: placeholder while loading | Helper loading test | Unit | AC text; `…` matches the Tags page |
| AC12: unit tests; existing tests pass | 17 new tests; existing payee unit and e2e tests pass | Unit + E2E | AC text |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** the refresh logic after merge, undo and sync has no test harness in the repo, so merge and merge-undo were checked by hand. Undoing a transaction delete, coming back to the page after adding or deleting a transaction, and the page staying usable while counts load weren't checked at all. Layout and styling will be covered by the VRT screenshots once regenerated.

**AI-written tests:** all 17 new tests were written by Claude Code. Their expected values come from the acceptance criteria and the agreed decisions, not from the code's output. Breaking the SQL by hand made the split tests fail, and Stryker found one weak test, which was fixed. *Add how you personally reviewed them.*

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- **Counting logic is in SQL.** It's faster, but mutation testing can't check it, so the server tests are its only protection.
- **Speed on large budgets wasn't measured,** and there's no database index for the payee lookup.
- **The two queries can briefly disagree** (the trade-off above).
- **Translations:** the rules column width fits English labels; a longer translation can misalign a row.
- **The refresh logic has no automated tests.**
- **Stryker configs and the merge script are course-only files.**

**Encountered:**
```

```markdown
# 1. Comment for issue #149 (Open Questions decisions)

🤖 Decisions on the Open Questions, as built in #189:
```

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
